Not a bank · Not advice · Just typograph

defects: Brand identity absence: the 'warm paper/ink/gold, hand-drawn Unown glyphs, dark-first' directive is completely ignored in favor of a cold, sterile white fintech default.
Contrast violation: the 'RUNWAY' section label in the top card row is nearly invisible (light gray on white), failing WCAG AA legibility standards.
Spacing rhythm failure: excessive vertical padding in the transaction table rows creates a sparse, washed-out feel that contradicts the 'calm density' requirement.
Crispness degradation: the hand-drawn aesthetic of the line graph is lost, appearing as thin, aliased strokes rather than intentional ink on paper.
Lack of visual hierarchy: headings (e.g., 'In, out, and the net between') and labels compete for attention; key data points aren't differentiated with weight or size.
Alignment issues: the top KPI card row has inconsistent baseline alignment for sub-labels (some on one line, some on two).
improvements: Adopt dark-first UI with warm paper/gold accents to match brand.
Increase heading weight and establish a clear type scale for hierarchy.
Tighten transaction table row padding for calm, intentional density.

critiques.label: The company's money, in plain figures
defects: The giant spike in the cash-flow chart visually dwarfs all other data points, making the rest of the 90-day series invisible and breaking the visual hierarchy of the graph area.

The red/green badge system (e.g., '▼ 42.5%') is not only low-contrast against the off-white background but also fails WCAG AA for accessibility, relying on color alone to convey meaning without sufficient contrast or text alternatives.

The typography scale for the sub-labels under the KPI cards (e.g., '4 accounts · seeded fixture Q4 FY26') is too small and light gray, making it nearly illegible and creating a weak secondary hierarchy tier.

The horizontal scrubber bar at the bottom of the chart is visually disconnected from the data visualization above it, sitting in its own isolated row without a clear spatial relationship to the graph, which fragments the interaction model.

The right-aligned metadata next to the 'In, out, and the net between' heading (date, in/out/net values) is misaligned with the heading's baseline and feels tacked-on, disrupting the calm density of the section header.
improvements: Scale the chart Y-axis to normalize the spike, making the 90-day trend legible and hierarchically balanced.
Increase the contrast of red/green badges and add textual cues (e.g., 'DECREASE') for WCAG AA compliance.
Unify the vertical spacing between the chart, scrubber, and legend to create a cohesive interactive module.

critiques.label: In, out, and the net between
defects: The 'In, out, and the net between' H1 is set in a bold sans-serif that completely breaks from the established mono/serif type discipline, creating a jarring tonal shift.
The right-aligned summary text ('30 Oct 2026 · in $47.4k...') on the section header line suffers from low contrast and is visually disconnected from the main title on the left.
The vertical whitespace between the scrub slider control and the 'TRANSACTIONS' subheader is excessive, disrupting the vertical rhythm and making the two components feel like unrelated islands.
The 'Where it went' H2 is nearly the same visual weight and size as the H1 above it, failing to establish a clear, stepped type hierarchy.
The line for 'Vercel' at the very bottom of the viewport is clipped, indicating poor consideration for scroll affordance or row padding, making the table feel cramped.
improvements: Align H1 and H2 type scales to the mono or serif font stack for consistent brand voice.
Reduce vertical whitespace between the scrub slider and the transactions section header to tighten rhythm.
Increase row padding and add a bottom scroll indicator to the transaction list to prevent clipping.

critiques.label: Where it went
defects: Eyebrow label 'TRANSACTIONS · THIS MONTH' is barely legible, rendering at ~50% contrast against paper and collapsing the visual hierarchy that 'Where it went' should anchor.
Typeface is a plain monospace sans with no display voice—zero trace of the hand-drawn Unown-glyph, warm ink, or gold brand system; the section reads like a default terminal dump.

Status pills ('settled', 'pending', 'failed') are the only color moments but feel accidental; 'pending' in muddy beige and 'failed' in washed red neither read as semantic signals against the light background, hurting WCAG contrast.
Currency amounts are right-aligned but inconsistent: negative values carry a '−' while positives don't, breaking the tabular figure rhythm and making the AMOUNT column visually jagged.
Row rhythm is loose—the generous top/bottom padding fights the thin 1px dividers, producing accidental double-rule density that feels like a print stylesheet leaked into a desktop app.
improvements: Introduce a display typeface and brand-glyph markers to reclaim visual hierarchy.
Unify the type scale, tighten row padding, and add semantic status colors.
Right-align figures with consistent sign glyphs and stronger eyebrow contrast.

critiques.label: Four buckets, one position
defects: Complete absence of Unown brand identity: no hand-drawn glyphs, no warm paper/ink/gold palette, no Game-Boy-inspired components; reads as a generic Figma template.
The 'Four buckets, one position' heading is visually detached and too close to the table above, creating a confusing vertical rhythm that fails to group the section logically.
The 'DISCLOSURES' section uses a muddy grayish-green background that clashes with the neutral whites of the cards and reduces the legibility of the fine print.
Low-contrast typographic choices: the gray 'settled' pill on white and the light gray account masks (9417 ••••) likely fail WCAG AA standards for body text.
Inconsistent card density: the four account cards feel sparse and floaty compared to the cramped disclosure text below, breaking the 'calm density' requirement.
improvements: Inject Unown brand: apply warm paper background, gold accents, and hand-drawn glyph icons to all buckets.
Increase vertical spacing before the section heading and use a darker, high-contrast background for disclosures.
Standardize the type scale: increase contrast on micro-text and align card metadata with a strict baseline grid.

critiques.label: The fine print, on purpose
defects: The hand-drawn Unown-alphabet glyph identity (the brand's stated core) is completely absent from the visible viewport — no glyph markers in the ACCOUNTS header, card labels, or disclosure section, leaving the 'fine print' section visually generic and off-brand.

Typography lacks a disciplined scale: the tiny monospace-looking 'ACCOUNTS' and 'DISCLOSURES' eyebrows, the heavy black 'Four buckets, one position' heading, the card titles, the tabular-numeral card values, and the small grey disclosure paragraph create at least 6+ conflicting type voices with no clear ratio, breaking the 'warm paper/ink' feel for a cold, default-system look.

Color and contrast are flat and low-contrast: near-black text on near-white with grey secondary text and only a faint sage-green pill; no 'warm paper/ink/gold' palette is present, and the light-grey card borders and 'settle' text fail to establish a legible, intentional dark-first hierarchy.

Spacing rhythm is broken by the large empty paper-white gap between the 'Four buckets, one position' card row and the full-width 'DISCLOSURES' panel, and the inconsistent vertical padding between section eyebrows, headings, and content creates an uneven vertical cadence.

The footer line 'Ledger — a design fixture…' is misaligned and visually disconnected: the left text and the right-side 'Not a bank · Not advice · Just typography' sit at different optical baselines with no container or rule tying them together, and the orange 'Read the build contract.' link clashes with the stated ink/gold palette.
improvements: Redraw the whole section in the dark-first paper/ink/gold palette with WCAG-legible contrast and gold accent lines.
Rebuild a strict 3-step type scale: large ink heading, warm-mid card labels, small mono disclosure text.
Unify vertical rhythm with consistent section padding and collapse the dead gap before disclosures.

defects: Type scale is monotonous: every major heading ('The company's money...', 'In, out...', 'Where it went') sits at the same ~32px weight, flattening the visual hierarchy
The 'Runway' metric card is the only one without a colored delta badge, creating an inconsistent visual rhythm in the KPI row
The 80-day cash flow chart has zero axis labels or gridlines, making the data completely uninterpretable to users who aren't already experts
The 'scrub days' interaction label and the chart legend sit on separate lines, creating awkward vertical whitespace that breaks the section's density
Status badges use low-contrast muted colors (pale green 'settled', pale amber 'pending') that fail WCAG AA against the light card background
improvements: Implement a distinct type scale: 40px for page titles, 28px for section headers, smaller for card labels
Add explicit gridlines and Y-axis labels to the cash flow chart for data interpretability
Increase contrast of status badge text and background to meet WCAG AA standards

defects: The transaction table's column spacing is uneven; the 'MERCHANT' column cramps the category labels (e.g., 'Infrastructure', 'Revenue') too tightly under the name, breaking the left-aligned rhythm.

The 'SCRUB DAYS' slider row has weak visual hierarchy; the grey track and muted labels cause it to vanish into the white background, making the 'net / inflow / outflow' legend below feel disconnected.
The 'Four buckets' card list suffers from vertical crowding; the 8-digit account numbers and sub-headers feel too close to the card borders, creating a noisy, uncalibrated vertical rhythm.
The top 'Open an account' button's terracotta red is the only saturated color on a monochromatic, warm-grey canvas; it feels jarringly out of place without a secondary accent to balance it.

In the disclosure section, the legal text block is set in a slightly larger, less legible typeface than the rest of the page, and the line-height is too tight for the dense text, violating WCAG-legible contrast at small sizes.
improvements: Standardize table cell padding to 12px vertical to recover lost breathing room in the 12-row list.
Increase scrubber and legend contrast with a darker, gold-tinted track and 500-weight labels.
Break the four-bucket card content into a stricter 4px-base spacing grid for calm density.

critiques.label: The company's money, in plain figures
defects: The main headline wraps so that 'plain figures' is split across two lines with 'figures' orphaned on its own, breaking the section's visual entry point. | 'figures' in top-left
Label rows like 'NET CASH FLOW, 30D' use wide-tracking monospace that feels inconsistent with the otherwise serifed, hand-drawn brand language. | upper card labels

The delta chips (▲ 12.7%, ▼ 42.5%) are small, low-contrast, and visually disconnected from the headline numbers; the green/red fills sit on a near-white card with weak WCAG contrast. | delta chips inside each card

Spacing rhythm between the eyebrow label, the large figure, and the meta line is inconsistent across cards — Cash Position has tight label-to-figure gap while Net Cash Flow is slightly looser. | vertical gaps in each card

Cards are separated by 1px lines that disappear at the bottom of the viewport, creating a ragged lower boundary that reads as an unfinished crop rather than a deliberate section break. | bottom card edge
improvements: Rewrap headline to 'The company's money, in plain figures' on two balanced lines.
Raise delta chip text to 13px min, use solid ink on tinted background for 4.5:1 contrast.
Unify card label typeface to match brand; keep monospace only for figures.
Set consistent 20px label-to-figure and 12px figure-to-meta spacing across all cards.
Give cards a soft warm border and 24px inter-card margin to read as discrete blocks.

critiques.label: In, out, and the net between
defects: The transaction table's 'AMOU' header is clipped, suggesting a lack of right-padding or a fixed-width constraint that fails on mobile viewports.
The 'SCRUB DAYS' control is visually weak; the label and track are too low-contrast against the paper background, lacking affordance.
The chart's single prominent spike (outflow) dominates the visual field, making the 'net' and 'inflow' data nearly invisible, failing to communicate the 'between' promise.
Vertical rhythm is inconsistent: the gap between the subtitle and the card is tighter than the gap between the card and the next section header.
The monospace font used for data (dates, values) is slightly too small, reducing legibility on smaller mobile screens.
improvements: Fix table column widths to prevent header truncation and ensure responsive fit.
Increase contrast and stroke weight of the scrub control for clarity.
Scale chart Y-axis to normalize spikes, improving visibility of baseline trends.

critiques.label: Where it went
defects: Right-aligned 'AMOUNT' column is hard-clipped, cutting off values and column header
Vertical rhythm is inconsistent; row heights and text baselines feel random
Monospace dates are set in a light gray that lacks WCAG contrast against the off-white background
Primary merchant names are too small and lack strong weight to lead the visual hierarchy
Hand-drawn ink style is not visible, causing a brand disconnect with the Unown aesthetic
improvements: Unclip right column, expand viewport padding to reveal complete currency values
Establish strict baseline grid, align row text to consistent vertical rhythm
Darken date text to #555+ for legibility, increase merchant name font weight

critiques.label: Four buckets, one position
defects: The monospace numerals ($1,284,600) clash with the brand's hand-drawn Unown aesthetic, feeling like a standard dev tool rather than a bespoke interface.
The '9417 **** 3382' account identifiers use an extremely light gray that likely falls below WCAG AA contrast thresholds, making them difficult to read on the white card background.
The vertical gap between the 'ACCOUNTS' eyebrow and the main heading is inconsistent with the tight vertical rhythm seen inside the cards below.
The cards are visually identical in structure and weight, failing to establish a visual hierarchy for the primary 'Operating' bucket versus secondary items like 'Tax'.
The lack of any visual texture or 'ink' in the card backgrounds feels sterile and contradicts the 'warm paper' brand description.
improvements: Increase the opacity of the account number text to at least 45% black for legibility.
Introduce a subtle border highlight or gold accent to the first card to establish visual priority.
Reduce the spacing between the eyebrow and main heading to improve typographic grouping.

critiques.label: The fine print, on purpose
defects: The section eyebrow 'ACCOUNTS' is illegible and disconnected from the 'Four buckets' title, failing visual hierarchy.
The 'fine print' card titles use a clean sans-serif, while the amounts use a crude monospace typeface that looks like a terminal default, destroying the warm brand cohesion.
The 'Payroll' card lacks a visible amount row that is present in every other card, creating a fatal inconsistency in the repeating pattern.
The vertical spacing between the four white cards is nearly zero, making them read as one blurry block rather than distinct, tappable entities.
The overall palette is a cold, low-contrast gray on white, completely missing the 'dark-first' and 'ink/gold' aesthetic mandated for the Unown brand.
improvements: Apply a strict dark-mode palette with high-contrast warm gold accents to the cards.
Standardize a single, legible display typeface across card headers and data values.
Add explicit 16px top and bottom spacing rhythm between every individual card container.
